items.title: Claude Williams interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 4, 1995
items.q: So that was Freddie Green I mean he stayed with the Count for forty years or something after that. But Freddie couldn’t — I was playing good guitar. After I left there...

ctx.x: When did you do your first recordings?

Well I really didn’t get to record too many, I think one session with Count. And it was interesting, because after we got to New York, John Hammond you know he also told Count about me because he had some of his boys had been through Peoria, Illinois and I had been playing at a hotel there. And they checked on me playing fiddle and guitar, I played some of both. So I was playing guitar. And after we got to New York, John Hammond had promised some musicians there, you know, the first chance I get I’ll put you with…
And you have quite a reputation as playing that fiddle, too.

items.title: 68097_Freddie Green oral history interview
items.q: He had a guitar player, Claude Williams. ... And, I made the audition with him, and got the job, more or less.

ctx.x: Basie didn't bring any guitar player?
He had a guitar player, Claude Williams. Yes. Guitar and violin.
